1.1: Paul opens up with love and authority—called by God, not by resume. He ain't movin' solo either—Timothy right beside him.
1.2: This letter ain't just for Corinth—it's for all Achaia. God's grace and peace? Ain't limited. He's for everybody who calls His name.
1.3: Paul praises God not just for being powerful, but for being the God of all comfort. Not "some." Not "sometimes." All.
1.4: Real recognize real: the same comfort God gives you? He expects you to pass that on.
1.5: Paul's like, "We been through it—but that pain was so we could comfort you." That's ministry: your suffering becomes someone else's survival kit. 🛟
1.8: Paul keeps it a buck—they was feelin' death close. No sugar-coatin' it.
1.9: But that moment taught 'em not to trust in themselves, but in God who raises the dead.
1.11: They made it through by prayer and the support of others. Reminder: your prayers might be the reason somebody else keeps going. 🙏🏾
1.12: Paul's flex is this: "We been real with y'all. What you see is what you get."
1.13: He wasn't tryna act deep or come with tricked-out theology. He stayed grounded, sincere, and led by grace.
1.14: He's sayin': Y'all our people, and we yours. Our wins are tied together.
1.15: Paul claps back soft: "Just 'cause I didn't show up when y'all expected don't mean I was bein' flaky."
1.20: He reminds 'em: God's promises ain't "maybe." They all "YES" in Christ. ✅
1.21: That same God confirmed Paul, sealed him, and gave him the Holy Spirit as a down payment. So yeah—he's serious about this.
1.24: He ends by sayin', "I ain't tryna control y'all's faith. I just wanna see y'all stand strong in joy." That's real shepherd energy. 🐑

2.1: Paul says, "Look—I ain't wanna show up with heavy vibes. I already wrote y'all with tears, not to hurt you but to let you know how deep my love runs."
2.2: This ain't cold leadership—it's that I'll cry over you before I cut you off kind of love.
2.3: Paul ain't out here for emotional whiplash. He wants them built up, not broken down.
2.4: Real leadership knows when to pull up, and when to pull back. 💬
2.5: Paul brings up the situation from 1 Corinthians (the dude wildin' with his dad's wife). He basically says, "Aight, he been checked, now it's time to bring him back."
2.7: "Don't let him drown in guilt," Paul says. Y'all disciplined him. Cool. Now hug him, not haunt him.
2.8: Forgiveness ain't a sign of weakness—it's spiritual warfare.
2.10: Paul flips it: "If y'all forgive him, I forgive him. Let's not give Satan no open doors—we ain't ignorant of his games."
2.11: Unforgiveness ain't protection—it's participation in the enemy's trap. 🧠⚔️
2.12: Paul lands in Troas to preach. The door's wide open—God clearly got favor there.
2.13: But he's restless. Why? Titus ain't there. This shows Paul's heart again. Even in ministry success, he values connection. You can be "effective" and still feel off if your crew ain't whole. Ministry without relationship feels empty.
2.14: Paul flips the energy and starts worshippin' mid-paragraph: "Thanks be to God—who always leads us in triumph in Christ."
2.15: He calls believers the fragrance of Christ: To some, we smell like life. To others, we smell like death.
2.16: Translation: the gospel gon' hit different depending on who hearin' it. But either way—we carry the scent. 👃🏾🔥
2.17: He ends like, "We ain't out here peddlin' the Word for profit. We say what we say with sincerity, straight from God." In a world full of talkers, Paul stood out 'cause his life matched his letters.

3.1: Paul's like, "Do I need to show up with a reference letter? Nah—y'all are the proof."
3.2: He says, "You're not written on stone like the old law. You're written on hearts—living epistles."
3.3: Translation: Your life is the letter. And folks are reading you even if they never open a Bible. 📖👀 Don't just quote Scripture—live like a page from it.
3.4: Paul says, "Our confidence? It ain't in ourselves. It's in God."
3.6: He makes it plain: God made us capable to serve this new covenant, not based on legalism, but Spirit. The old law kills. The Spirit? She gives life. ✨ This ain't about perfection. It's about presence.
3.7: Paul throws it back to Moses, when his face lit up after being with God—but that glory was temporary.
3.8: He's sayin', "If that old thing had shine, how much more glory does the Holy Spirit bring?"
3.9: The old covenant brought rules & judgment. The new one? Righteousness & transformation. You ain't just tryin' to obey—you're bein' made new. 🔁
3.12: Because we got this kind of hope? We speak boldly.
3.13: Paul says Moses had to cover his face so people wouldn't see the glory fade—but folks still out here wearin' spiritual veils.
3.16: That veil? It only gets lifted when you turn to Jesus. You can know Scripture and still be blind if you ain't lookin' through the lens of Christ. 👀
3.17: Paul drops a heavy bar: "The Lord is Spirit. And where the Spirit of the Lord is... there is freedom."
3.18: And with unveiled faces, we're lookin' right at God's glory—like a mirror. But it don't stop there. We're being transformed—from glory to glory. Level to level. Real change. This ain't behavior modification. This is Spirit-led identity shift. 🔥

4.1: Paul starts off: "We got this ministry because God showed mercy—so we ain't quittin'."
4.2: He's sayin', "We don't do manipulation, sneakiness, or scripture-twisting." They not on no performative ministry vibes. Everything out in the open. If you gotta scheme to spread the gospel, you ain't really preachin' Jesus.
4.3: If the gospel still feel hidden? Paul says it's hidden from those perishing.
4.4: The "god of this world" (aka Satan) got folks blinded, blocking them from seeing the light of Christ. The enemy don't mind you being religious—as long as you never really see Jesus.
4.5: Paul makes it plain: "We don't preach us—we preach Jesus as Lord."
4.6: They're just servants. Jesus is the point. And that same God who said "let there be light"? He lit us up too—put that light inside so we could reflect His glory. The shine on your life? Ain't about you—it's about Him. 🔦
4.7: This the meat of the chapter. Paul says: "We got this treasure in jars of clay."
4.8: Why? So nobody gets it twisted—the power ain't from us. It's from God. And then the real talk starts: Pressed on every side—but not crushed. Confused—but not outta options.
4.9: Persecuted—but not abandoned. Knocked down—but not knocked out.
4.10: They carry the death of Jesus in their bodies so His life can show up too.
4.12: Your weakness ain't disqualifying you—it's qualifying you to be a real carrier of His power. 💥
4.13: Paul quotes, "I believed, therefore I spoke."
4.14: They believed in resurrection power—so they ain't stay silent.
4.15: Their suffering wasn't just for them. It was bringing life to others, and thanksgiving to God.
4.16: Paul brings it home: "We don't lose heart." Even though the body's breakin' down, the inner you is being renewed daily.
4.17: He calls it a "light affliction"—for a moment—working eternal weight of glory.
4.18: Last bar hits hard: "We don't focus on what's seen—it's temporary. We fix our eyes on what's unseen. That's eternal." Faith ain't about ignoring pain. It's about seeing through it.

5.1: Paul keeps it 100—this body? It's just a tent, a temporary setup.
5.2: But when it folds? We got a heavenly home, made by God Himself, that don't wear out.
5.3: In the meantime, we groan. Not 'cause we wanna die—but because we want that eternal upgrade.
5.5: God's already prepped us for that with the Holy Spirit as the down payment. You feelin' the tension? That's the Spirit lettin' you know this world ain't your final address. 📦➡️🏠
5.6: Paul's like, "As long as we here in the body, we ain't fully home with the Lord."
5.7: That's why we walk by faith, not by what we see. Faith ain't fake. It just sees farther.
5.8: And honestly? Paul says he'd rather be absent from the body and fully present with the Lord. That's the goal. 🎯
5.9: Whether we here or with Him, our aim is simple: please God.
5.10: 'Cause one day? Every one of us gotta stand before the judgment seat of Christ. We'll all answer for what we did—good or bad. Salvation is a gift. Rewards? That's stewardship. 🔍
5.11: Knowing how serious God is, Paul says, we persuade folks.
5.12: They ain't out here to impress or perform—they just want people to know Jesus, no matter what it look like.
5.13: Some folks think they wild or too bold—but Paul's like: "If we extra, it's for God. If we chill, it's for y'all."
5.14: The love of Christ is what drives us—because we believe this:
5.15: Jesus died for everybody, so now, we don't live for ourselves anymore—we live for the One who died and rose again. 🙌🏾
5.16: Paul says, "We don't judge anybody by appearances anymore." Even Jesus—we used to see Him through a human lens, but we on spiritual timing now.
5.17: And then this bar that shook generations: "If anyone is in Christ, they a new creation. Old things gone. New has come." Not improved. Not touched up. NEW. 🔁✨
5.18: Everything we have is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ.
5.19: And now? He gave us the same job—ministry of reconciliation. God ain't holdin' people's sins over them—He extended grace.
5.20: And now we're His ambassadors, beggin' folks: "Be made right with God."
5.21: Final verse hits deep: "God made Him who knew no sin to BE sin for us, so that we might become the righteousness of God." That's the divine exchange. That's the gospel. Period. 🔄✝️👑

6.1: Paul starts with a plea: "Don't waste the grace God gave you."
6.2: He quotes God like, "I heard you at the right time. Help came on the day of salvation." Then he adds: "That time? Is right now." Don't just receive the Word—respond to it. This ain't the season to sleep. This is the moment. ⏳🔥
6.3: Paul says, "We do our best not to give anybody a reason to discredit this ministry."
6.4: Then he rolls out a wild list of what ministry really costs: Patience in pain, Beatings, Prison, Sleepless nights, Fasting, Being talked about—good and bad.
6.6: But also: Living with pure hearts, Moving in real love, Speaking the truth, Relying on God's power, Holding on to righteousness on both sides.
6.8: Then he hits us with a contrast bar: "They call us imposters—but we're real. We get ignored—but we're known. We feel like we're dying—but look—we still alive." This section is the résumé of a faithful servant. Don't let the platform fool you—this walk ain't for the soft-hearted. 💔🛡️
6.11: Paul's like, "We been wide open with y'all—our hearts are stretched toward you."
6.12: He tells the Corinthians: "You not restricted by us—you're holding yourselves back."
6.13: So he says, "Open your heart too. Let it be mutual." Vulnerability in ministry gotta go both ways. You can't grow where you won't open. 🧠❤️
6.14: This the famous "Do not be unequally yoked" section—but Paul ain't just talkin' about dating. He's saying: "Watch your alignments."
6.15: Righteousness got nothing in common with lawlessness. Light don't blend with darkness. Christ ain't sittin' at the same table as Belial (another name for the enemy).
6.16: Paul reminds them: Y'all are God's temple. God said: "I'll live in them. I'll walk with them. I'll be their God, and they'll be My people."
6.17: So what does He ask? "Come out from among them. Be separate. Don't touch what's unclean. And I'll receive you."
6.18: "I'll be a Father to you—and you'll be My sons and daughters."

7.1: Paul closes out the last thought and opens this one with a challenge: "Since we got these promises, let's cleanse ourselves." Not just from dirty habits—but from toxic spirit-level stuff too. And how do we do it? With reverence for God, not just religious routine. Real holiness don't just show up in your behavior—it shows up in your heart posture. 🧼🛐
7.2: Paul's basically sayin: "We ain't wronged or finessed nobody. We ain't toxic. Open up to us again." He reminds them: "You in our hearts. If we gotta die together or live together—we locked in."
7.4: Then he switches gears: "I'm talkin' bold, but it's 'cause I'm proud of y'all. I'm comforted. I got joy even in the middle of tribulation." This is real pastoral energy—correctin' without cancelin'. 🫂
7.5: Paul gets honest—he was restless. Outside: pressure. Inside: anxiety.
7.6: But God—the One who comforts the down bad—brought Titus through.
7.7: And not just Titus—but the good news he carried about the Corinthians: Their desire to see Paul, Their grief over what went wrong, Their zeal to make things right. That report lit Paul's spirit all the way up. 🔥
7.8: Paul keeps it real—he ain't happy they were sad, but he is glad that their sorrow led to change. "That letter hurt y'all for a minute. But it led to repentance? Worth it."
7.10: Godly sorrow brings you to your knees and gets you back on your feet. Worldly sorrow just leaves you in your feelings with no forward motion. Tears don't impress God—transformation does. 💧➡️🔥
7.11: Paul lists all the signs their repentance was real: Diligence, Clearing the air, Righteous anger at sin, Fear (of the Lord), Desire to do better, Zeal, Vindication. That ain't surface-level sorry. That's full-on turnaround energy. 🛑↩️
7.12: Paul clarifies: "I didn't write that letter just for the one who sinned or the one who got hurt. I wrote it to show y'all how deeply we care."
7.14: Titus is feelin' refreshed by how they received him, and Paul's joy is overflowing 'cause everything he said about them proved true. That's restored trust, not just reestablished rules.
7.16: Paul closes like, "I'm so glad I can have confidence in y'all again." That's full circle grace.

8.1: Paul brags on the churches in Macedonia like, "Y'all, they was broke... I mean broke-broke... and still gave generously." Not just giving from overflow—but from a place of lack, pressure, and pain. They wasn't forced—they was beggin' to give.
8.5: First they gave themselves to the Lord, then they gave what they had. That's the order: heart before hands. ❤️➡️✋🏾
8.6: Paul says, "Titus started this mission in y'all, and I want him to help finish it."
8.7: Then he hits 'em with this bar: "Y'all already great in faith, speech, knowledge, passion, and love. Now go ahead and excel in giving too." He's sayin'—don't be spiritual in word and stingy in action. 🗣️💰
8.8: Paul keeps it a buck: "This ain't a command—it's a heart check." He's like, "Let me test your love by comparing it to what others have done."
8.9: And then he drops that Christ reminder: "Jesus was rich, but made Himself poor for your sake—so y'all could be spiritually rich." So the question ain't "how much can I give?" It's: "How can I reflect that kind of love?" 💸➡️✝️
8.10: Paul reminds them: "Y'all had the desire to give last year—now finish what you started." Willingness matters more than amount. God looks at what's in your hand, not what ain't.
8.12: It's not about matching others—it's about moving in obedience.
8.13: Paul's like, "I ain't tryna put you in a bind so somebody else can chill." He's talkin' about equality—how your abundance now can help their lack, and vice versa one day. It's not redistribution—it's kingdom rhythm.
8.15: Then he quotes the manna story: "He who gathered much had nothin' left over, and he who gathered little had no lack." God's math? Everyone eats. 🍞
8.16: Paul brags on Titus again, sayin', "He got the same heart I do—and he comin' with backup." There's another brother with him who's respected in all the churches and chosen to travel with the gift.
8.20: Paul's like: "We doin' this above board—so nobody can accuse us of shady handling." "We not just keepin' it clean for God—but for people too." Ministry money gotta come with ministry-level integrity. 💼🙌🏾
8.24: He wraps up by sayin': "Show these men—and the churches—that your love is real and our braggin' on you wasn't wasted."

9.1: Paul's like, "Y'all already know the deal—I really ain't gotta say much." He's been hypin' up their generosity to the Macedonians, and now he's like: "Don't make me look goofy. Y'all said y'all was ready—be ready."
9.5: He's sending the brothers ahead so the gift is prepped—no last-minute scrambling. This ain't about pressure. It's about making sure your giving is from the heart, not from the hustle. 💛📦
9.6: One of the coldest giving bars in the Bible: "Whoever sows sparingly will reap sparingly. Whoever sows bountifully will reap bountifully." Giving is planting. What kind of harvest you want? Then match it with your seed. 🌱➡️🌾
9.7: Paul's like, "Don't give outta guilt or routine. Give from a place of purpose." God ain't lookin' for grumpy generosity—He loves a cheerful giver. If you ain't smiling, don't swipe it. 😅💳
9.8: Paul assures them: "God can flood you with all grace. You'll have what you need—and enough to bless others too."
9.9: He quotes: "He gave freely to the poor, and his righteousness lasts forever."
9.10: He says: God supplies seed for the sower AND bread for food—He got both the supply and the harvest.
9.11: And what's the end goal? That your giving causes others to give thanks to God. Your generosity ain't just a transaction—it's a testimony. 🙌🏾
9.12: This gift? It's doing two things: Meeting needs of the saints and Multiplying gratitude to God. Your obedience shows folks you ain't just talkin' faith—you walkin' it.
9.14: And now the people you blessed? They gon' be prayin' for you, grateful for the grace God showed through you. That's kingdom economics. Giving leads to prayer, praise, and purpose. 🔁💥
9.15: Paul can't help himself. He ends the chapter in worship: "Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift." Like... all this talk about giving? Just a shadow of what God already gave in Jesus. You'll never outgive God. Ever.

10.1: Paul opens soft: "I'm coming to you in the meekness of Christ." But then he hits 'em with: "Don't make me have to get bold when I show up."
10.2: Some folks been tryna play Paul like he tough in letters but timid in person. Paul like: "Don't try me. If I gotta be bold in person, I will." Gentleness ain't weakness—it's restraint. 🧘🏾‍♂️
10.3: Paul breaks it down: "Yeah, we in human bodies, but we don't fight like the world fights."
10.4: Our weapons? Not bullets, fists, or IG clapbacks. They're mighty through God to: Pull down strongholds, Shut down arrogant arguments, Take thoughts captive to Christ.
10.5: This is mind renewal, not just mindset shifts. You don't win spiritual battles with petty energy—you win with God's power. 🧠⚔️🕊️
10.7: Paul checks their discernment: "Y'all judging by outward appearance. If somebody think they belong to Christ—so do I."
10.8: Paul says if he gotta boast in his God-given authority, he will. And he reminds them: "That authority wasn't given to tear you down—it's to build you up."
10.10: And to those sayin' he only sound tough in letters? "What I say in my letters, I'll do in real life too. Don't test it." Don't mistake a quiet anointing for a passive assignment. 📜➡️🗡️
10.12: Paul throws subtle shade at folks who compare themselves to themselves: "That ain't wise. We don't measure our calling by man-made standards."
10.13: He says, "I'm not out here claiming other folks' territory. We planted the gospel in y'all—this is our lane."
10.15: He's hoping their faith grows, so the reach can grow too. Not for ego—but to spread the gospel beyond Corinth. Stayin' in your assignment? That's where the favor flows.
10.17: Paul closes this chapter by bringing it all back to God: "If you gon' brag, brag in the Lord."
10.18: The ones God approves? Ain't the ones hypin' themselves up. It's the ones God puts His stamp on. You don't need to be verified by people if you've already been appointed by God. ✅🙌🏾

11.1: Paul's like, "Y'all gon' have to bear with me while I vent a little."
11.2: He compares himself to a spiritual father tryna keep his daughter (the church) pure for Christ—but she out here flirtin' with false teachers.
11.3: He says, "Just like the serpent tricked Eve, I'm scared y'all being deceived too."
11.4: They out here entertaining: Another Jesus, A different spirit, A fake gospel. And the worst part? They puttin' up with it. 😤 Paul's like, "Y'all more loyal to lies than to the truth you first received."
11.5: Paul says, "I might not speak like a scholar, but I ain't lacking in real knowledge."
11.6: He didn't come with a TED Talk—he came with truth and integrity. Don't confuse stage presence with spiritual weight.
11.7: Paul's like, "I humbled myself and preached to y'all for free. Was that wrong?"
11.8: He didn't ask them for money—but got support from other churches to serve them.
11.9: He says, "I didn't burden y'all, and I won't start now."
11.11: Then he drops this bar: "God knows I love y'all. Don't confuse distance with disloyalty."
11.12: Paul says he gonna keep doin' what he do to block the fakes from getting a foothold.
11.13: He calls them what they are: False apostles, Deceitful workers, Clout-chasin' con artists.
11.14: And he breaks it down: "Don't be surprised. Even Satan shows up lookin' like light."
11.15: So of course his crew gon' show up lookin' holy too. But the end? They gon' reap what they sow. Not every shiny ministry is Spirit-led. Some of it is just demonic with a logo.
11.16: Paul's like, "Y'all tolerate fools, so let me act a little foolish for a second."
11.20: He calls out how they've let: Folks enslave them, Take advantage, Talk down to them, Physically disrespect them.
11.21: He's like, "Y'all been loyal to abuse but skeptical of real love." Sometimes church folks love chains more than change. ⛓️➡️🕊️
11.22: Paul's like, "They Hebrews? Me too. Israelites? Me too. Abraham's kids? Same."
11.23: But then he shifts: "Are they servants of Christ? I go harder than them. And not with titles—with scars."
11.24: His résumé is pain: Beatings, Imprisonment, Shipwreck, Hunger, Danger from everyone: Jews, Gentiles, nature, fake Christians, No sleep, No food, Constant pressure.
11.28: And on top of that? "I carry the daily burden of caring for the church."
11.29: "When y'all weak, I feel it. When y'all fall, I burn inside." That's spiritual fatherhood, not platform ministry.
11.30: Paul says, "If I'm gon' boast, I'm boasting about my weakness."
11.32: Then he shares a wild story—he had to escape a city in a basket through a window to avoid arrest. That ain't glamorous. That ain't empire-building. That's real obedience under pressure.

12.1: Paul says, "Boastin' ain't really helpful... but lemme tell y'all somethin' wild." He shares a story—but in third person, like, "I know a man..." That "man" is him. He just too humble to say it outright.
12.2: He talks about bein' caught up to the third heaven—aka the throne room of God.
12.4: He heard things too deep, too holy to even repeat. He could brag about that... but he won't.
12.5: He'd rather boast in weakness than visions. Real ones don't need clout—they carry conviction. 🔒🔥
12.7: Paul says, "To keep me from gettin' big-headed from all this revelation, I was given a thorn in my flesh." He don't say what the thorn is—but it hurt. It humbled. It harassed.
12.8: He begged God three times to take it away...
12.9: But God said: "My grace is enough. My power works best when you weak." So Paul flips it: "Cool then—I'll brag on my weakness. That way Christ's power can rest on me."
12.10: "When I'm weak? That's when I'm really strong." Bro... that's kingdom math: Less of me = more of Him. 🩹➕👑
12.11: Paul's like, "Y'all made me go here. I shouldn't have had to defend myself."
12.12: He's done more than enough to prove he's an apostle—signs, wonders, and endurance.
12.13: He hits 'em: "Only thing I didn't do? Ask y'all for money. Forgive me for treating y'all different." That's Paul with sarcasm—but also hurt. He gave without asking. And got questioned for it. Sometimes the ones you pour into the most... forget it cost you everything. 💔
12.14: Paul says, "This my third time coming. And still—I don't want your stuff. I want you."
12.15: He sees himself like a parent, storing up for the children—not the other way around. "I'll spend everything for y'all—even if the more I love you, the less I get loved back." Whew. That's real shepherd pain.
12.17: He says, "Did I ever take advantage of you? Did Titus? Didn't we walk with integrity?" Love gives without leverage.
12.19: Paul says, "We ain't just defending ourselves—we're doing everything for your edification."
12.20: But he worried. He's like: "I might pull up and find stuff like: jealousy, arguing, gossip, pride, impurity, wild behavior..."
12.21: And if so? He knows it'll break him. He'll grieve. Not 'cause they failed—but 'cause they didn't repent. What hurts a real leader ain't the fall—it's when folks stay down and refuse to get back up. 😔

13.1: Paul's like, "I'm pullin' up for the third time now." And just like the law says: "By the mouth of two or three witnesses every word gets established."
13.2: He ain't comin' to play. He already warned them before, and now he says: "If folks still wildin' when I get there, I won't spare nobody." Grace is still in the room... but so is accountability.
13.3: They been wantin' "proof" that Christ is really speakin' through Paul? He's like: "You gon' see it."
13.4: And don't get it twisted: Christ looked weak when He was crucified, but He's alive by God's power. And we look weak too, but we walk in that same power. Weakness ain't the absence of God—it's often where He shows up most. 🔋
13.5: Paul flips it heavy: "Y'all keep tryna check me. Check yourselves." He's like: "Are you really in the faith? Run that self-test. Unless you failin' it and don't even know."
13.6: But he's confident—they'll pass. He's not just throwin' shots—he's callin' them higher. Spiritual maturity starts with a mirror, not a microphone. 🪞
13.7: Paul says, "I'm prayin' y'all don't do wrong—not so I look good, but so you stand right."
13.8: He's not tryna win debates. He wants them to win in obedience.
13.9: And if that means Paul looks weak but they stay strong? He's good with that. That's kingdom leadership. Less ego, more edification.
13.10: Paul's lettin' 'em know: "I'm writing this now so that when I come, I don't gotta come with heat." His authority wasn't to destroy—it was to build. Some folks confuse correction with cruelty. Paul? He just tryna build without breaking.
13.11: Paul wraps like a real one: "Finally, fam—be complete. Be encouraged. Be on one accord. Live in peace." Why? Because when you move like that, the God of love and peace gon' stay with you. 🕊️💞 That's not just a farewell—that's a spiritual promise.
13.12: He says: "Greet one another with a holy kiss." That's deeper than culture—it's about love in community.
13.14: He closes with what we now call a benediction: "The grace of Jesus, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with y'all." That's the whole Trinity showin' up for your soul. ✝️❤️🔥
